headline: The gold grants provisional credit to only 3 of 4 qualifying disputes because it counts disputes filed earlier in the same conversation toward the 'no more than 2 in 12 months' rule; that reading is defensible but not the only one, and it also depends on filing order.

issues.summary: Four disputes qualify by reason: Costco dup $312.87, Costco fraud $234.56, Amazon dup $215.67, Amazon fraud $129.45. The user has zero prior disputes. The gold marks the first three filed eligible and the Amazon fraud ineligible, which only works if criterion 4 counts disputes filed earlier in this session. Reading criterion 4 against the pre-existing history (0) makes all four eligible.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_015: "4. Previous Disputes: The customer has not filed more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months"
db.json transaction_disputes: no rows for user 01f21c9970 (only dsp_7a3e91b4c2d8 for 6680a37184); get_user_dispute_history_7291 returns 'No transaction disputes found for this user.'
gold[9].arguments: txn_2f16599b9075 unauthorized_fraudulent_charge, eligible_for_provisional_credit false; gold[6..8] eligible true
Replay: setting gold[9] eligible=true changes the DB hash (verified)
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that checks history once and finds 0 prior disputes marks all four eligible and fails the exact-hash comparison. The gold's reading is supported by the literal text (when the 4th is filed, 3 disputes have been filed in the past 12 months), and get_user_dispute_history_7291 would show the in-session filings, but a reasonable agent can read 'previous' as pre-existing history.
issues.suggested_fix: State in doc_015 that disputes filed earlier in the same interaction count toward criterion 4, or make the history-only reading gold (all four eligible).

issues.summary: Under the gold's in-session reading, criterion 4 counts ALL disputes, including reason-ineligible ones. The final eligible set therefore depends on filing order. The gold only results if the three largest reason-eligible disputes are filed before any other dispute; filing in the customer's listing order (Costco fraud, Costco dup, Costco not-as-described, ...) leaves only two eligible.
evidence: user_scenario step 8: "If there's any limit on provisional credit, I want it applied to the biggest charges first... Do not mention this if the agent does NOT bring provisional credit up."
In user listing order the 5th filing (Amazon fraud) sees 4 prior and the 6th (Amazon dup $215.67) sees 5 prior, so both are ineligible: 2 eligible vs the gold's 3
issues.why_it_matters: Even an agent that adopts the gold's reading must plan to file the three largest eligible disputes first. The tie-break preference surfaces only if the agent raises provisional-credit limits with the customer.
issues.suggested_fix: Define the cap as 'at most N provisional credits per 12 months' and let the customer's priority choose which ones, independent of filing order.

issues.summary: Several stored values have no scripted customer answer: resolution_requested for each dispute (gold: partial_refund $50 for the incorrect-amount charge, full_refund otherwise), the replacement's shipping address (gold: registered home address), and expedited shipping (gold: true). The natural simulator answers match the gold (a $50 overcharge, free expedited on a Gold card recommended for fraud), but none is scripted.
evidence: user_scenario has no resolution, shipping-address, or expedited step (steps 4 and 6 are missing)
gold[15]: "shipping_address": "4532 Magnolia Lane, Philadelphia, PA 19103", "expedited_shipping": true
issues.why_it_matters: If the simulator improvises differently (e.g. 'full refund on everything'), the record differs. This is simulator variance rather than an agent error.
issues.suggested_fix: Script the resolution per transaction and the shipping preference in the user scenario.

solution_check: Verification: 4 fields given. Transaction ids from the DB: Costco 10/09 txn_a450807f1148, 10/23 txn_f7ce44574766, 11/04 txn_39469d5db822, 11/11 txn_02bf2e9dcfa7; Amazon 10/11 txn_2f16599b9075, 10/26 txn_182e896e1c97, 11/06 txn_b94ce7d77e7f, 11/13 txn_d8e6e3386b89. Reasons, merchant contact, and last-4 (1652) follow from the script and the tools. Gold card opened 06/15/2024, premium limit $10,000. Criteria 1/3/5 make all four fraud/duplicate disputes eligible; the gold's ineligible 4th comes only from in-session counting of criterion 4, combined with largest-first filing. The required read get_user_dispute_history_7291 is in the gold, so it's allowlisted: skipping it changes the hash (verified). Reordering the replacement before the disputes, or writing 50.00 for 50, leaves the hash unchanged (verified).
prior_note: The prior review called this a Blocker with gold inconsistent. I confirm the same provisional-cap defect but rate it Major: the literal criterion-4 text supports the gold's in-session count, so the gold can be reached by a reasonable reading. I also add the filing-order dependence and the unscripted values.
notes: The 'duplicate' Costco $312.87 and Amazon $215.67 charges appear only once each in the DB (no second matching charge); no doc requires verifying a duplicate exists, so this doesn't change the gold. The dispute records copy the registered address and phone from the DB. Verifiers may reasonably argue Blocker if they judge the history-only reading the dominant one.
